verdict.line: You lose if you let Urgot poke you down with his passive and Corrosive Charge before level 6; you win if you survive to six and time Feast off a landed Rupture-Feral Scream combo.

brief.thesis: Urgot's ranged kit (Echoing Flames procs on autos and Purge, plus Corrosive Charge at range 800) and his E (Disdain) shield mean he controls trades at range and punishes any premature approach, which is why OP.GG calls the lane his even though the 100-game head-to-head sits at an even 50%. Cho'Gath's Q (Rupture) actually outranges his Corrosive Charge at 950, letting you poke back from max range before 6, and once R (Feast) comes online at level 6 you have a point-blank true-damage finisher his kit has no answer to if you land it while his E is down.

theirWindow.what: He can shield through your Q (Rupture) and E (Vorpal Spikes) damage while poking you with his passive (Echoing Flames) and Q (Corrosive Charge). Don't walk up for extended autos here — trade at Q range and back off.

yourWindow.when: His E (Disdain) just missed or is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Engage immediately: Q (Rupture) to slow, W (Feral Scream) to silence his Q/W response, then stack autos for Vorpal Spikes damage. From level 6 onward, close with R (Feast) for the true-damage finish.

Feast online, but his R threatens executes too

start.why: The mana and sustain let you hold Vorpal Spikes trades and keep casting Rupture into his poke without running dry, which matters since he wins the pure range war pre-6.

boots.why: His passive (Echoing Flames) and Purge are both physical, repeated-hit sources — flat physical reduction blunts both far more than Mercury's Treads does here.

core.why: Stacks health that directly feeds Feast's max-HP growth and keeps your autos (and Vorpal Spikes procs) relevant as you tank his sustained Purge.
Gives you damage that doesn't depend on sticking to a kiting Urgot, since he'll disengage with Disdain if you commit.
The shield and grievous wounds proc directly counters his sustained auto-attack damage from passive procs and Purge.

situational.when: he builds into on-hit or crit and you need the armor plus healing cut
he's kiting you with Corrosive Charge and you need to close the gap faster
you need a dash to combo into Rupture-Feast before his E resets
the game goes long and you want more magic damage and sustain in extended skirmishes

runes.keystoneWhy: The proc heal and bonus health let you absorb his passive and Corrosive Charge poke instead of losing the lane purely to chip damage before you have Feast online.

summoners.why: Teleport resets you after losing early poke exchanges and gets you back for turret plates; Flash lets you dodge or follow up on Disdain and close distance for a clean Feast.

playing.title: Poke first with Q
playing.detail: Rupture's 950 range beats his Corrosive Charge's 800, so you can land free damage from max range before he can respond in kind pre-6.

playing.title: Save W for the all-in
playing.detail: Don't burn Feral Scream on wave clear — hold it to silence his Q/W mid-fight once you're committed to a trade.

playing.title: Track his Purge rank
playing.detail: Purge's cooldown drops from 12s to 0s by rank 5, meaning late-game he can unload it almost on demand — don't assume it's down just because he used it recently.

playing.title: Punish a whiffed Disdain
playing.detail: His E is 16-14s on cooldown and is his only shield/disengage — engage immediately when it misses or gets used offensively.

playing.title: Don't overextend pre-6
playing.detail: Without Feast you have no burst finisher, and his ranged poke adds up over a full trade exchange.

playing.title: All-in when Q and E are both down
playing.detail: Chain Rupture's slow into Feral Scream's silence, then auto for Vorpal Spikes stacks, finishing with Feast once in range.

playing.title: Respect his ultimate threshold
playing.detail: Fear Beyond Death reaches 2500 range and executes low-health targets, so don't sit under half HP even when you're ahead in the fight.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, and win rates above are measured from live games on the current patch; the core item path has a small sample (4 games) so treat it as directional. The mechanical reasoning — timing windows, range comparisons, and cooldown reads — is my own analysis, not sourced from the data.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid being hit with (P) and (E). Keep your distance while using [Q] to gain the upper hand in combat. Try to kill him after reaching level 6.
